artworks.title: Apollo and Daphne
artworks.description: Bernini catches the instant of Ovid's metamorphosis — bark closing over Daphne's flesh as Apollo's hand still grasps what is already becoming laurel.

artworks.title: Diana and Actaeon
artworks.description: Titian's National Gallery/Scottish National Gallery canvas — Actaeon stumbling on Diana's bath, the glance that will grow antlers in Ovid's Book III.

artworks.title: Apollo and Daphne
artworks.description: Waterhouse's Pre-Raphaelite chase — Daphne already sprouting laurel as Apollo reaches, Ovid's pursuit restaged for the Edwardian gallery.

artworks.title: Apollo and Daphne
artworks.description: Pollaiuolo's early Renaissance panel — the god and the nymph mid-flight as branches replace arms, Metamorphoses I in tempera.

artworks.title: The Death of Actaeon
artworks.description: Titian's late National Gallery canvas — Diana's arrow and the hounds closing on the hunter already half stag, Ovid's punishment completed.
